text:
lia: FYI I'm opening a PR to refresh the Error Reference entries for 429s, timeouts, and context-limit fallbacks. PR will include short SDK snippets (JS + Py), a migration note for Dedicated customers, and a small QA checklist. Need reviews from @jamal and @sasha.

jamal: TL;DR: do we want the snippets to show header-based retry (Retry-After) or just client-side exponential backoff?

sasha: both. show a tiny `Retry-After` example and a client config example. keep each snippet <=10 lines. add a note about when to prefer server-driven vs client-driven retries.

lia: Agreed. Draft snippet for JS (fetch + Redwood client config):

lia: ```js
// handle 429 with Retry-After or client backoff
const res = await fetch('/v1/generate', opts);
if (res.status === 429) {
  const retryAfter = res.headers.get('Retry-After');
  if (retryAfter) await sleep(Number(retryAfter) * 1000);
  else await backoffSleep();
}
// client config example
client.configure({ retries: { maxAttempts: 4, backoff: 'exponential', jitter: true } });
```

marko: For the client sample, can we use `client.configure(...)` exactly? we still have slight naming differences in SDKs. maybe call it `client.updateRetries(...)` for the JS snippet so it doesn't mismatch in copy/paste.

lia: good point — I'll make the method name intentionally generic: `client.setRetryPolicy(...)` in docs to avoid exact API drift.

jamal: For timeouts/context limits, add a tiny Python snippet showing prompt trimming + resumable conversation hint. Example: trim oldest messages first and signal truncated context to caller.

lia: python snippet:```py
# trim oldest messages to fit token budget
def trim_history(history, max_tokens):
    while estimate_tokens(history) > max_tokens:
        history.pop(0)  # drop oldest turn
    return history

# send with metadata flag so caller knows we trimmed
client.generate(messages=trim_history(history, 2048), metadata={'context_truncated': True})
```

sasha: Nice. Add a short note under "Fallback behavior" that when context is trimmed we prefer graceful degradation (shorter answer) over failing with 413/timeout. Link to the graceful-degradation playbook.

lia: I've updated links but noticed one redirect is stale: `/docs/fallbacks` currently 302 -> `/guides/fallbacks` which then 404. Marked to fix. @marko can you open an infra link-fix ticket for the redirect?

marko: Will do. I'll create a ticket and add that to the PR checklist.

docs-bot: CI: docs-lint failed on `error-ref/429.md` — missing example caption and `language` codeblock tag.

lia: Thanks — will patch. Also adding a tiny automated test note for the QA harness: run `docs/tests/error-ref/429-smoke` to validate snippets compile (py + node).

jamal: For the migration note (Dedicated): we need to call out per-route quota bumps and that Dedicated customers may need to update their routing policy to route to a higher-capacity pool instead of retrying aggressively. Short blurb under "Dedicated migration" will suffice.

lia: I'll add a 2-paragraph migration note and a one-liner config example showing `routePolicy: { fallback: 'higher_capacity', maxClientRetries: 3 }`.

sasha: +1. If you want I can do a quick copyedit pass for tone and length after you push the PR.

lia: pushing in ~30m. tagging this thread in the PR description for traceability. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

marko: ping me if the redirect ticket blocks the PR merge; otherwise I'll batch the infra change into next release.

lia: noted — will include a temporary inline note in the PR pointing to the redirect ticket so reviewers know it's tracked.

docs-bot: NOTE: please run `yarn docs:build` locally and add a screenshot of the rendered 429 page to the PR for reviewers to sanity check the snippets.

lia: doing that now — will attach screenshot and CI smoke log.

jamal: LGTM for scope. thanks!
